newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed on Tuesday following Wall Street's 43-point drop on Monday as European investors awaited a batch of corporate results.
"It's been a boring morning. There wasn't much news overnight so there hasn't been any reason to do too much," one market maker said.
"I think the Dow will start a few points better today and then all eyes will be on the bonds."
U.S. treasuries were becalmed as the market braced itself for this week's auctions. The June T-bond was down 1/32 to 107-20/32.
The yield on the cash 30-year long bond stood at 7.10 percent by 1025 GMT.
Later on Tuesday $17 billion in two-year notes go under the hammer followed by $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.
Rising bond yields helped spook U.S. investors on Monday, sending the Dow Industrials Average 43.34 points lower to 6,660.21.
"If U.S. interest rates go up over the next few months the market is going to start worrying about future earnings growth," one dealer said.
Oil stocks were mostly higher following better-than-expected earnings reports on Monday from Exxon Corp and Amoco Corp.
Texaco Inc, which is expected to book a $488 million tax refund in its first quarter results, due later on Tuesday, was up $5/8 to $105.

The company said on Monday it would receive a total refund of $700 million from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service(IRS)after the U.S. Supreme Court refused an application from the IRS to review a lower court decision in Texaco's favour.
Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp, which were also due to announce Q1 figures on Tuesday, were up $3/8 to $125-7/8 and $1/4 to $65 respectively.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.85 to 765.00.
